speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how often has the raw water quality been unacceptable for our water treatment plants in Johor since they have been in operation; (b) how did that affect the supply of water to Singapore and Johor; and (c) what is the mitigation plan going forward.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Johor also has water treatment plants along the Johor River, upstream of the Johor River Waterworks, and will shut down their plants when pollution occurs upstream of them.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given the importance of the Johor River to the water supply of both Singapore and Johor, we have expressed our concern over the frequent recurrence of pollution incidents to Malaysia, both at the federal and state levels.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Most recently, at the Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat in April, Prime Minister Lee raised concerns over pollution in the Johor River and the severe impact of pollution incidents on both countries.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do so on a goodwill basis without prejudice to our rights under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During these pollution incidents, PUB works closely with the Johor authorities to flush the polluted water column from the Johor River.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Such collaboration between PUB and its Johor counterparts has helped us to manage the pollution incidents.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB conducts stringent water quality tests to ensure that the raw water from the Johor River is suitable for treatment before resuming abstractions and operations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Nevertheless, pollution incidents along the Johor River impact the water supply of both countries and remain a serious concern.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to engage our Malaysian counterparts on the need for them to take measures to prevent future pollution incidents along the Johor River.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: How vigorously do we check on the quality of the water from Johor?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: And lastly, does Singapore have any say on the factories' waste discharge in Johor that ends up in the reservoirs supplying water to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Both Singapore and Johor authorities check the water very vigorously.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, we are usually alerted by of our counterparts in Johor that the water is polluted, either with ammonia or other contaminants, before the water comes to us because the Johor plants are upstream.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And indeed, they have to close down their plants before we do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And maybe a few hours or a few days later, in coordination with our counterparts, we turn up operations at our plants.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are not in control of how their land is allocated or where factories are.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we certainly are in collaboration with both their Department of Environment as well as their waterworks to make sure that should incidents like this occur, alerts can be given early enough for both parties to act.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
